name: Carrell Moto Classic
description:
A proper motorcycle jacket in full-grain synthetic bovine leather — the kind that breaks in over years and smells like machine oil and rain. Asymmetric zip closure, snap-down lapels, two chest pockets and a zippered utility pocket on the left sleeve. The shoulders are pre-shaped with a slight forward roll that looks natural on almost any frame. Available in black, oxblood, and a dark tobacco brown that ages beautifully.

Carrell has been making this jacket in essentially the same pattern since 2140. It's not fashionable in any particular direction — it simply exists as a correct object. You see it on Shelf riders who've saved up for months, on Tier 3 commuters who've owned theirs for a decade, on the occasional Tier 4 person who wants something that doesn't look like money.
what_it_says: You bought something once and intend to keep it. You know the difference between a real jacket and a fashion jacket.
worn_by: anyone who wants a jacket that lasts
story_hooks: A jacket passed down from a dead courier contains a hidden interior pocket sewn shut — something is inside.
Carrell has quietly discontinued this model; the remaining stock is being bought up by someone, systematically, across every outlet in the Tier 2 corridor.
The tobacco brown colorway was a limited dye lot from a single supplier who has since vanished — jackets in that color are becoming collector's items on the secondary market.

physical_description.visual_profile: A classic asymmetric moto jacket with authentic proportions—structured shoulders with forward roll, nipped waist, and hip length. Projects timeless functionality over trend. The silhouette reads as purposeful and broken-in rather than pristine.
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the shoulders and torso with enough ease for layering and movement. Pre-shaped armholes sit naturally on most frames. Hip-length cut allows freedom over utility pants or thermals.
physical_description.primary_material: Full-grain synthetic bovine leather—engineered to age like genuine hide, developing patina and subtle creasing over years of wear
physical_description.texture: Smooth grain surface that gradually softens with use; develops a matte patina in creases and contact points. Oil-resistant finish that repels rain while absorbing workshop grime.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in three timeless options: deep black (most common), oxblood red (classic moto choice), and dark tobacco brown (ages to burnished cognac). Minimal branding or accent stitching.
physical_description.closures: Asymmetric full-length zip with substantial metal slider; snap-down lapels for chin protection or relaxed wear
distinctive_features: Two chest pockets with snap closures—deep enough for tools or documentation
Zippered utility sleeve pocket on left arm—practical, worn-in appearance
Pre-shaped shoulder construction with forward roll—anatomically correct
Minimal branding—only small Carrell Goods Co. woven label inside
Designed to develop visible creasing and darkening at stress points
Heavy-duty stitching visible at seams and pocket attachment
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 aspirational to Tier 2 practical—accessible to working-class buyers but not ostentatious. Used examples hold value across all tiers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf riders saving for months, career commuters with decade-old jackets, and anyone rejecting disposable fashion. Signals practical durability and anti-trend values. Common on courier pilots, mechanics, transit workers, and independent operators.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in gradually from stiff and creaky to supple and lived-in. Older jackets show oil stains, worn edges at cuffs, darkened creases, and softened grain. Patina is expected and valued.
